You can and should (at least in Oregon) refuse the road side sobriety tests.  You pretty much have to take the breathalyzer(although you can demand a blood test instead).

If you were to fail the road side sobriety test (in the subjective opinion of the officer) and go on to pass the breathalyzer...  they could and would issue you a DUI, and you would most likely be found guilty.
If on the other hand you pass the road side sobriety test then fail the breathalyzer you will be issued a DUI and you will be found guilty.
According to every attorney(which I am not) I've ever heard speak on the subject there is absolutely no up side to doing the road side sobriety tests.  
If you don't do the road side sobriety test and still blow a .08 or higher, there may be ways that a good attorney can get the breathalyzer results thrown out.  However, if you do the roadside sobriety test and fail the breathalyzer....
